key_insight: Co-PiLOT turns inverse design into constrained latent-space optimization by using a generative decoder as a feasibility prior and a physics-informed optimizer to search for target microstructures efficiently.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical way to design magnesium alloy microstructures and textures under expensive crystal-plasticity simulation constraints, making it useful for computational materials and solid mechanics workflows.
method: ViT-based encoder compresses EBSD microstructure images into a low-dimensional latent space.
Generative decoders (latent diffusion / DiT / rectified flow) reconstruct high-fidelity candidate microstructures from latent codes.
MERIDIAN performs active optimization with deep-kernel GP uncertainty, feasibility prediction, manifold-aware trust regions, and target-aware acquisition.
evidence_signal: On an ~80,000-image EBSD dataset, ViT-FMDiT achieved the strongest reconstruction quality (FID 27.86, MS-SSIM 0.178) and, with MERIDIAN, reduced relative target error by 3–22% versus seven baselines within 160 simulations.
watch_item: Performance depends on decoder fidelity and solver coupling, so any domain shift or weak reconstruction could constrain feasibility and transferability of the latent optimization results.
paper_title: Co-PiLOT: Constrained Physics-Informed Latent Optimization for Target-Driven Inverse Design
